title: Your Boots Jump Before You See the Stick, Yet Your Conscious Brain Learns Last
description:
Behavioral & Circuit Analysis — Joseph LeDoux (1994-2000): The 12-Millisecond 'Low Road' vs 'High Road' to the Amygdala — & Why Fear != Freeze, grounded in Joseph E. LeDoux (1995) (Annual Review of Psychology). Empirical findings show that in the late 1980s and 1990s at NYU (synthesized in 1995 and 2000), Joseph LeDoux asked a puzzle that baffled sensory physiology: if you remove an animal's entire auditory cortex, why does it STILL freeze instantly to a fear-conditioned warning tone?.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how thalamus, amygdala, primary visual cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that while the amygdala reacts to isolated sensory triggers, contextual safety discrimination (telling a snake behind zoo glass apart from a snake on your porch) depends on hippocampal and ventromedial prefrontal inputs gating the amygdala.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Joseph E. LeDoux (1995). Emotion: Clues from the Brain. Annual Review of Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.ps.46.020195.001233
- Joseph E. LeDoux (2000). Emotion Circuits in the Brain. Annual Review of Neuroscience. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.neuro.23.1.155
- Michael T. Rogan, Ursula V. Stäubli, Joseph E. LeDoux (1997). Fear conditioning induces associative long-term potentiation in the amygdala. Nature. https://doi.org/10.1038/37601

AI Disclosure: Visual reenactments, 3D anatomical models, and narration in this documentary Short were produced with AI synthesis tools from verified peer-reviewed sources.
